newsitem.title: BELGIUM: SOCCER SHOWCASE-LOWLY EKEREN STUN PROUD ANDERLECHT.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER SHOWCASE-LOWLY EKEREN STUN PROUD ANDERLECHT.

text.p: Unfancied Ekeren overcame a two-goal deficit to stun eight-times winners Anderlecht 4-2 after extra time and win the Belgian Cup for the first time in their history on Sunday.

The plucky Antwerp side refused to die after conceding two goals to their aristocratic opponents but Anderlecht had only themselves to blame for squandering a hatful of second half chances that could have killed off the game.

Swirling wind and driving rain hampered both sides in the opening stages but Anderlecht should have been 3-0 up before Ukrainian striker Oleg Yaschuk opened the scoring after 31 minutes, glancing home a header from a corner.

Ten minutes into the second half Ghanaian international defender Samuel Johnson looked to have made sure of the trophy, tucking a low left-foot shot inside the far post after Ekeren failed to clear a free-kick.

Desperate to lift the cup and put some shine on a disappointing season, Anderlecht, and Yaschuk in particular, had numerous chances to seal their win but let Ekeren back into the game midway through the second half with a stunning own goal.
Johnson, hero-turned-villain, attempted to clear a harmless long pass but sent a diving header flashing past his own goalkeeper Geert De Vlieger from 10 metres.
Spurred on by this change in their fortunes, Ekeren pushed forward, brought on their "super-sub" Alex Czerniatynski and equalised with just five minutes left.
Florian Urban advanced over the halfway line, feeding Czerniatynski on the right. His near-post cross was met by Gunther Hofmans whose volley was beaten out by De Vlieger.
Cvijana Milosevic hammered the rebound goalwards where Johnson headed off the line. But the ball fell to Ekeren winger Christophe Kinet who buried his shot from 10 metres.
Substitute Ervin Kovacs should have finished off the job for Ekeren in the last minute but headed tamely past the upright with the goal at his mercy.

A minute into extra time, Ekeren went ahead for the first time, with Kinet and Hofmans working a one-two on the edge of the box to feed Canadian international Tomasz Radzinski who, unmarked, made no mistake with his short-range header.
Four minutes later Hofmans crowned Ekeren's historic day, shooting low past De Vlieger to make it 4-2.
Anderlecht, who tried desperately to turn the tide in the dying minutes, with efforts from Johnson and Johan Walem hitting the woodwork, were not the only losers.

Lommel, who finished fifth in the Belgian league, had hoped to win a UEFA Cup berth if Anderlecht qualified for the Cupwinners' Cup. Anderlecht, who finished fourth in the league, will now take the final UEFA slot.
Defeat was only Anderlecht's third in 11 cup final appearances. They last lost 20 years ago when Ekeren were still playing in one of the nation's lower regional divisions.
Ekeren, who trounced Anderlecht 4-1 in the league last month, had lost their two previous finals, in 1990 and 1995.
"This is a big victory for a small club," said Jos Verhaeghen, chairman of Ekeren, who have been in Belgium's top flight for only eight years.
"We knew we would stand a good chance if we went into extra time. We had been working hard in the past weeks and we were in superb shape," he said.
Anderlecht coach Johan Boskamp was clearly disappointed.

"We had chances to finish them off when we were 2-0 up but we failed. We had so many opportunities," said Boskamp, who has led Anderlecht to three league titles in five years but is now moving to Ghent.
